record.file_problem: Repository material only: metadata, README, and file list; the linked paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports measurements of SAE encoder-direction geometry and RLHF-related activation changes after abliteration, but it does not measure refusal or capability outcomes. Those measurements do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The README reports its own proxy-geometry and activation-change results. It explicitly identifies abliteration-completeness and pre-topk/post-topk validation as unresolved; it gives no observed refusal rate, direct test of harmful-request compliance, harmless-request refusal, or general capability after abliteration. Its noted classification accuracy concerns prompt-level discriminability, not refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The README reports SAE encoder-direction geometry and activation-change metrics on one abliterated Qwen3-8B checkpoint. It reports no refusal rate, no ablation/addition effect on refusal, and no capability measure, and says abliteration completeness is unverified ("Critical Gap 1 (BLOCKING)"). Its results bear on RLHF-imprint preservation, a different construct, so it tests no version. It uses abliteration as a tool and argues from it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. One addition: the authors also flag that 45.4% of directions have slope above 1, which contradicts their own geometric account.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE encoder-direction metrics and geometric comparisons on an abliterated checkpoint, rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction intervention and behavioral tests. The repository describes itself as research/paper material, not a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported measurements vary by layer (20 versus 22); the README also says generalization across abliteration implementations is untested.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-500 RLHF-sensitive SAE encoder directions keep their RLHF-induced changes after abliteration: Reversal Score mean 0.921, OLS slope near 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration (huihui-ai v2, Qwen3-8B) leaves RLHF-induced SAE encoder-direction activation changes largely intact, conditional on abliteration completeness.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction has mean |cos| about 0.02 with RLHF-sensitive encoder directions at layers 20 and 22.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is nearly orthogonal to RLHF-modified SAE encoder directions in Qwen3-8B.

fits_no_version.finding: In the RLHF-sensitive subspace, the abliterated model's centroid is closer to instruct than to base, more so than in control subspaces. 64.6% of these directions also respond to benign prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliterated models keep instruct-like representations in RLHF-sensitive subspaces, mostly reflecting general stylistic RLHF changes.

record.problems: The README says abliteration completeness has not been verified and conditions its main findings on it. It also identifies missing z_pre/z_post validation, an unexplained amplification result, and absent bootstrap confidence intervals for centroid ratios. No refusal or general-capability outcomes are reported in the README.
record.rows_left_out: None of the README's stated core geometric and centroid results were omitted. The downstream classification accuracy=0.476 is not included as a row because it is a prompt-discriminability result, not a measure of refusal or the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No causal ablation or addition of a difference-in-means direction with refusal or capability outcomes.
No refusal-rate measurement of the abliterated checkpoint; completeness is explicitly unverified.
Multi-dimensional refusal subspace is listed as future work (PCs 1–3 not measured).
No harm-judgment versus refusal separation test.
No transfer test. Base/instruct centroid comparisons concern RLHF features, not the refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: This is an automated AI-generated research repository, not peer-reviewed, and only the README was read. The README states that refusal-rate verification is blocking, so no behavioral evidence exists. The title's claim that abliteration "cannot erase RLHF" is not a claim about refusal removal (V2), and should not be read as challenging it.

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition test of a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, refusal behavior, or other capabilities.
No measured refusal outcome for the released abliterated checkpoint; completeness is explicitly unverified.
No attack or training-against-ablation robustness test.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple directions; extension to a multidimensional refusal subspace is listed as an open question.
No separation test of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing.
